# one-pi-one-price

> One currency. One price. A clear explanation of why a single, freely tradable asset cannot have two different prices.

## Summary
This repository explains the simple principle: "A currency cannot have two prices."
It focuses on the Pi Network discussion about mined vs bought Pi, showing the difference between fairness and market mechanics, and how arbitrage enforces price unity.

## Core Thesis
- One currency = One asset = One price in an open market
- Mined Pi and bought Pi are the same asset
- Effort differs, but the unit is identical
- Arbitrage naturally converges prices across linked markets
- "What is fair" is different from "what the market does"

## Key Files
- README.md: Overview and TL;DR
- docs/ONE-CURRENCY-ONE-PRICE.md: Core principle with real examples
- docs/MINED-VS-BOUGHT.md: Effort vs capital
- docs/ECOSYSTEM-VS-OPEN-MARKET.md: Internal vs open market
- docs/OUSD-AND-SETTLEMENT.md: Settlement vs direct cash-out
- docs/ARBITRAGE-ENFORCES-ONE-PRICE.md: How one price is enforced
- docs/FAIRNESS-VS-MARKET.md: Fairness vs market reality
- docs/FAQ.md: Direct answers
